stem: What is the characteristic gait and posture of a child affected by SCFE?

options.text: Limping with an out-toeing foot position
Walking on the balls of the feet
A stiff-legged gait with no knee flexion

explanation: The fixed external rotation deformity of the hip joint causes the patient to walk with a limp and turn their toes outward.
rationale: Consider the effect of a fixed 'external rotation' deformity on the foot's direction.

optionExplanations.A: The fixed external rotation deformity of the hip joint causes the patient to walk with a limp and turn their toes outward.
optionExplanations.B: The hip deformity in SCFE is characterized by external rotation, which results in out-toeing rather than in-toeing.
optionExplanations.C: Toe-walking is associated with other conditions; SCFE typically presents with a limp and rotation of the leg.
optionExplanations.D: The primary deformity involves the rotation of the hip joint, affecting the orientation of the foot during a limp.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Limping with an out-toeing foot position
